question: What usable fish and waterbody evidence can be extracted from the two Apayao freshwater abstracts in the 2009 ISSAAS convention-summary issue without overstating their taxonomic, spatial, temporal or reuse resolution?

issue.title: Journal of ISSAAS, Volume 15, Number 2
issue.section: Abstracts of papers / ISSAAS Philippines National Convention 2009
issue.issueIndexClassification: The archive lists Volume 15 Number 2 (December 2009), an abstracts-of-papers link, and a free full-issue download. The FAO AGRIS record classifies the fish-and-shell item as Conference; Summary.
issue.reuseNotice: The archive site has a site-wide copyright notice. No item-specific license for the abstracts or underlying data was located; free access is not reuse permission.

abstracts.titleAsPublished: Fish and Shell Production Practices in Apayao Province
abstracts.affiliation: Apayao State College, Malama, Conner, Apayao
abstracts.scope: Province-level claim about native fish and shell species in Apayao freshwater habitats and fisherfolk production/capture practices.
abstracts.countInterpretation: Sixteen vernacular labels are printed under a combined fish-and-shell description. They are not 16 verified fish taxa or species; individual fish-versus-shell classification and scientific identities are unresolved.

abstracts.titleAsPublished: Bio-physical and Chemical Characterization of the River System in Apayao Province
abstracts.affiliation: Apayao State College, Malama, Conner, Apayao
abstracts.scope: The abstract names ten major Apayao rivers and reports field survey/water analysis plus a generic statement that fish and shell inhabit the rivers.
abstracts.taxonomicEvidence: No fish or shell taxa are named in this abstract. The general habitat statement cannot yield a species checklist or river-specific assertion.
abstracts.waterQualityInterpretation: The abstract makes a historical summary claim against DENR standards but gives no survey dates, station design, per-site results or underlying measurements in the abstract. Do not present it as a current safety or pollution assessment.

crossAbstractAssessment.independence: Both abstracts are in the same convention-summary issue and share authors/institution. Whether they draw on the same field campaign or data is not established; do not count them as independent surveys.
crossAbstractAssessment.temporal: 2009 is the publication/issue year, not a verified fieldwork date.
crossAbstractAssessment.spatial: Province-level freshwater habitat wording and ten printed river names are leads only. No boundary, coordinates or catchment crosswalk is supplied.
crossAbstractAssessment.taxonomy: No scientific-name determination is available from the inspected abstract pages; do not normalize vernacular names to species by guesswork.
crossAbstractAssessment.reuse: No item-specific data or article reuse license located; public app publication remains unapproved.

disposition.reason: The accessible material is conference-summary text only. Taxonomic identity, fish-versus-shell label allocation, dates, sites, methods detail, vouchers and reuse rights are insufficient for species, occurrence, geometry, safety or app publication.

followUpQuestions: Does Apayao State College hold the full survey/report, original questionnaires, photo documentation or data tables behind either 2009 abstract?
What were the field dates, exact sites/rivers, effort and station crosswalk for each abstract, and did the two abstracts rely on a shared survey?
Can each vernacular label be linked to the original language/community, fish-versus-shell category, identified specimen/photo and a scientific name determination?
Were voucher specimens deposited, and if so, what are their accession numbers and current custodian?
Are original 2009 water-analysis results available with site/date methods, and what separate rights apply to underlying data, photographs and text?
Can the college confirm item-specific attribution, redistribution, public display and potential commercial-use terms?

sources.supports: Official full issue PDF; abstract section; both Apayao abstracts and their printed pages, methods, names and stated limitations.
Official ISSAAS issue listing; Volume 15 Number 2 (December 2009), abstract and full-issue access labels, and archive copyright notice.
FAO AGRIS bibliographic record and duplicate summary for the fish-and-shell conference abstract; not an independent field dataset.
Publisher description of the Journal of ISSAAS; inspected page did not supply an item-specific reuse license for these abstracts.
